headline_marked: 36 deaths in July: [[Dengue cases and fatalities surge]] in Bangladesh
headline: 36 deaths in July: Dengue cases and fatalities surge in Bangladesh
summary: With 15,310 hospitalisations this year, experts warn that the outbreak could peak in September unless a coordinated national control strategy is adopted.
details: Dengue infections and deaths rose sharply in July, with 36 fatalities recorded compared to 13 in June. According to the Directorate General of Health Services, 54 people have died and 15,310 have been hospitalised so far this year.

Infections also surged in July, with 9,206 cases recorded, up from 2,903 in June. Bangladesh Shishu Hospital and Institute reported a significant increase in admissions, with 45 patients in July compared to 25 in June.
Entomologist Kabirul Bashar warns that the upward trend is likely to continue through August and into September, with daily cases potentially reaching 800 from early August.

Bashar noted that while heavy rainfall has temporarily reduced mosquito density in Dhaka, breeding is expected to increase again once the rain decreases. He stressed the need for source reduction and breeding-site management.

GM Saifur Rahman, assistant professor at National University, criticised the lack of a centralised, proactive mosquito control programme. He argued that the current fragmented approach is failing to produce meaningful results.
Rahman called for the establishment of a central mosquito control authority supported by expert entomologists to oversee and monitor prevention activities nationwide.
caption:
36 deaths in a single month. Dengue cases are surging in Bangladesh, and experts warn the peak may still be ahead.

Dengue infections and deaths rose sharply in July, with 36 fatalities recorded compared to 13 in June. According to the Directorate General of Health Services, 54 people have died and 15,310 have been hospitalised so far this year.

Infections also surged in July, with 9,206 cases recorded, up from 2,903 in June. Bangladesh Shishu Hospital and Institute reported a significant increase in admissions, with 45 patients in July compared to 25 in June.

Entomologist Kabirul Bashar warns that the upward trend is likely to continue through August and into September, with daily cases potentially reaching 800 from early August.

Bashar noted that while heavy rainfall has temporarily reduced mosquito density in Dhaka, breeding is expected to increase again once the rain decreases. He stressed the need for source reduction and breeding-site management.

GM Saifur Rahman, assistant professor at National University, criticised the lack of a centralised, proactive mosquito control programme. He argued that the current fragmented approach is failing to produce meaningful results.

Rahman called for the establishment of a central mosquito control authority supported by expert entomologists to oversee and monitor prevention activities nationwide.

#Bangladesh #Dengue #HealthAlert #PublicHealth #Dhaka

Source: Dhaka Tribune, The Daily Star
